evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/App.tsx:72 — MfaWrapper.verify() calls raw `fetch('/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify', ...)` with a HARDCODED root-relative path, bypassing the app's configured API base URL. Every other API call in ppt-web routes through a configured base: lib/api.ts:64 `DEFAULT_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'` (comment: 'In production VITE_API_URL must be set'), and contexts/AuthContext.tsx:97 `API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? ''` for the generated @ppt/api-client. The MFA verify fetch uses NEITHER env var.

Impact: in any deployment where the api-server is served from a different origin than the SPA (VITE_API_URL points at e.g. https://api.example.com/api/v1), the MFA challenge verification request is sent to the SPA's own web origin (`/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`) instead of the api-server, so it 404s and `response.ok` is false — MfaChallengeProvider treats every correct code as a failure and the user can never clear an MFA-gated mutation. MFA (N9) is a security-critical, user-facing auth path. Works only in same-origin/reverse-proxy deploys, silently breaks on split-origin deploys — a latent config-coupling bug and an inconsistency with the rest of the app.

Confidence medium: the hardcoded relative path is unambiguous on static read; whether it breaks depends on the deployment's VITE_API_URL being cross-origin (runtime/deploy-dependent). Fix: build the URL from the same base the rest of the app uses (VITE_API_URL / getApiClient()), e.g. `fetch(\`${import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'}/auth/mfa/verify\`, ...)` or route the verify call through getApiClient()/the generated api-client so the Authorization header and base URL come from one source of truth (mirrors the lib/api.ts request interceptor).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:321 — `export default getApiClient();` is evaluated eagerly at module import. getApiClient() (lines 273-278) lazily creates `apiInstance` via createAxiosInstance() with NO config, so the default-exported instance has `tokenGetter === undefined` and `onUnauthorizedCallback === undefined`. Later, AuthProvider calls configureApiClient() (AuthContext.tsx:352) which does `apiInstance = createAxiosInstance(config)` (api.ts:299) — a BRAND-NEW AxiosInstance. getApiClient() now returns the configured instance, but the default export still references the original, token-less one.

Consequence: any consumer that does `import api from '../lib/api'` (the natural default import for a file literally named `api`) holds an axios instance whose request interceptor has no token getter (no `Authorization: Bearer` header, api.ts:201-206) and whose response interceptor has no 401 handler (no silent refresh, api.ts:219-221). Its requests go out unauthenticated and 401s are never recovered — diverging from every feature hook that correctly uses getApiClient(). The module's own design (AuthContext.tsx:340-344 warns 'getApiClient() falls back to a default instance with no token getter') documents exactly this hazard, then re-introduces it via the eager default export.

Currently LATENT: a repo-wide grep found no default-import consumers of lib/api (all callers use the named getApiClient()), so no live request is affected today — hence severity low (+1). But it is a real foot-gun that will silently break auth the moment any future code adds `import api from './lib/api'`. Confidence medium (static-confirmed divergence; impact gated on a future import). Fix: remove the eager `export default getApiClient();` and either drop the default export or make it a lazy getter/proxy that always resolves the current `apiInstance` (e.g. export a Proxy delegating to getApiClient()), so there is a single configured instance.
